acceptance_test.text: Add a test that persists at least two structured FindingTransitionPayload records for one work unit whose natural mirror/history order differs from finding_id-lexicographic order, and assert authoritative_native_findings() does NOT raise when the two finding sets are content-equal but differently ordered, while still raising on genuine content divergence. If the mirror is already guaranteed sorted elsewhere, document that invariant next to the tuple-equality check.

new_findings.summary: ProductionWorkflowDriver.authoritative_native_findings() (src/orchestrator.py) compares the replay-derived projection against the state-v3 mirror with plain tuple equality: `if projected != mirror_findings: raise WorkflowExecutionError(...)`. `projected` is explicitly `tuple(sorted(findings.values(), key=lambda item: item.finding_id))` from replay_findings(), but nothing in the diff shows that `mirror_findings` (WorkflowHistory.findings, passed by _bind_authoritative_native_findings) is guaranteed to be maintained in finding_id-sorted order. Tuple `!=` is order-sensitive, so two content-identical finding sets that merely differ in element order could trigger a false-positive fail-closed halt. Every Slice 2 test exercising this guard or the full convergence path (mirror-drift tests, record-ahead-precedes-guard test, and all three end-to-end convergence tests) uses exactly one FindingRecord at a time, so this order-sensitivity is never falsified even though the plan anticipates multiple simultaneously tracked findings.

pre_mortem: If this approval is wrong, the most likely path is a future run with two or more concurrently tracked findings hitting the untested order-sensitivity in authoritative_native_findings()'s tuple equality: the mirror carries findings in insertion/update order while replay_findings() returns them sorted by finding_id, the comparison spuriously fails, and a legitimate combined-native run halts on a phantom 'state-v3 mirror' divergence -- undermining the guard's core guarantee, but only surfacing once a real multi-finding scenario occurs, since every test in this diff exercises just one finding at a time.

review_evidence.break_condition: This approval breaks if the attested full-matrix run does not correspond to the diff shown, if any cited combined-native test is later found absent, skipped, or non-passing, or if a concrete multi-finding run is shown to trigger the order-sensitive false positive described in C-05.
review_evidence.dimensions: (1) Combined bindings: authoritative_native_findings/_bind_authoritative_native_findings only engage when both native transports are bound; other runs are unaffected, and the new WorkflowDriver protocol method is guarded via getattr/callable. (2) Reviewer-owned authority: replay_findings() enforces reporter/severity immutability, requires opening metadata only on 'opened' and response_decision only on 'responded', rejects duplicate opens and orphan responses with stable codes; finding_payload() gates structured fields behind work_unit_id and preserves the legacy payload shape (verified by dedicated legacy/native shape tests). (3) Mirror fail-closed behavior: binding fires at all three role-invocation sites only when no record-ahead result was recovered, exercised by parametrized drift tests (CODEX_PLAN_REVISION and CODEX_CORRECTION), a Claude-review drift test, and inverse record-ahead-precedes-guard tests showing zero provider calls on drift and zero guard calls on successful recovery. (4) End-to-end convergence: three full round-trip tests (slice, plan revision, restarted final review) instrument every legacy parser to raise on any call and drive state through denial->correction->closure to the correct ANTIGRAVITY_* step with exactly one persisted disposition and the expected review count each. (5) Markdown projection: convergence table is built purely from the accepted record chain (work-unit-round-first-wins, unique fingerprints/decisions), never read back for decisions, verified by projection and audit_trail tests. (6) C-01 through C-04 closures (mirror guard scope, schema copy, plan_result compatibility, require_structured removal) are untouched by this diff and not invalidated by it.
review_evidence.largest_residual_risk: The state-mirror equality check is a plain tuple comparison against a sort-normalized replay projection, and no supplied test exercises more than one finding at a time, so an order-only mismatch between mirror and replay could produce an untested false-positive fail-closed halt in a real multi-finding combined-native run (finding C-05).
